transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ChatGPT. What brings you in today?

I go to great lengths to avoid getting on an airplane, even when it means missing important family events. It has gotten to the point where I'm missing out on my family's lives, and I just can't bring myself to do it anymore.
Do you mainly fear flying itself, or do you also avoid other situations like heights, enclosed spaces, or other specific places because they make you feel panicked or trapped?

It is really just flying that terrifies me, rather than heights or small spaces in my everyday life. The fear is specifically about being sealed in a metal tube at 30,000 feet with absolutely no way out. It is so tied to air travel that I even had to walk out of an art exhibit at a local airport when I realized I was too close to the gates, though other situations don't usually bother me.

When you think about flying, do you ever have sudden panic symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, or a feeling that you might die or lose control, or is it mainly the fear of the flight itself?

I experience both, to be honest. If my kids even mention buying a ticket, my heart starts pounding, my hands go clammy, and I vividly picture the plane dropping out of the sky. The fear of the flight itself is so intense that getting on a plane feels like signing my own death warrant at my age.
Do you have this intense fear only with flying, or do you also have similar fear and avoidance with other situations like driving, elevators, bridges, or public speaking?
No, I haven't really noticed those fears in other situations like driving or using elevators. My issue is strictly with flying; that's the only thing that brings on this kind of dread.
Have you had this fear of flying for at least 6 months, and does it happen only when you think about or have to take a plane?

Yes, this fear has been with me for a little over two years now, starting after a very turbulent flight shortly after my wife's funeral. It isn't a constant anxiety, but rather something that is strictly triggered when I have to think about flying, talk about buying tickets, or go near planes.
When you are not thinking about planes or travel, do you feel anxious or panicky in other parts of your life, or is the fear only triggered by flying and flight-related situations?

No, I don't feel anxious or panicky in other parts of my life at all. This intense dread is strictly tied to flying, thinking about air travel, or being near flight-related environments. Outside of those specific situations, I'm generally quite calm and don't experience these symptoms.
Do you fear flying mainly because you think you might crash or die, or is it more about having a panic attack or feeling trapped while on the plane?

It is actually a combination of both, if I'm being honest. The thought of being sealed in a metal tube at 30,000 feet with no escape is terrifying, but it also genuinely feels like signing my own death warrant. I often get these vivid, awful pictures in my mind of the plane dropping right out of the sky.
Do you have this same level of fear or avoidance in any other situations where you might be trapped or unable to escape, such as elevators, tunnels, bridges, or crowded rooms?

No, I don't experience that kind of fear in elevators, tunnels, or crowded rooms at all. My anxiety is strictly limited to airplanes and flying. I can handle those other situations without any trouble.

The fear is narrowly restricted to air travel and is not better explained by broader agoraphobic fears, generalized anxiety, or panic disorder.
